newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Labour Min rules out PM resignation -agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech Labour Min rules out PM resignation -agency.

text.p: Czech Labour and Social Minister Jindrich Vodicka, after meeting with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, said the PM would not announce his resignation at a news conference scheduled for 1200 GMT, the CTK news agency reported.
Vodicka, who is also a member of Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS), said Klaus would issue a "principle political statement", and added that the government was ready to carry on.
The prime minister's office would only say that Klaus called the news conference for 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) Friday to make an important statement.
Earlier in the day, opposition leader Milos Zeman called for a no-confidence vote against the government, which he said should be taken at the July parliamentary session.

Klaus's three-party coalition, which holds 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house, agreed Wednesday to budget cuts, public sector wage freezes, and other measures while acknowledging mistakes were made in their economic policy.

Klaus has been under intense pressure over the past two weeks amid a sharp downturn in the economy and heavy pressure on the Czech crown, culminating in the central bank being forced to float the currency on Tuesday.
The finance, industry and trade, education and interior ministers were changed as part of the Wednesday shakeup.
